translations.answer: Maintainers recommend using forwardKinematics(model, data, q, v, 0*v) to zero out the generalized acceleration, then directly read the frame's classical acceleration drift using getFrameClassicalAcceleration(); the original author confirmed this is the classical Jdot*qdot required in the formula. It only returns the product/drift term, not the full Jdot matrix. Subsequent users' matrix formulas without official confirmation should not be included in this closed-loop experience.
translations.applicability: Applies to scenarios where only the product/drift term of classical Jdot*qdot is needed; full Jdot or other frames must be handled separately.
translations.credibility.rationale: There is engineering record for environment, processing steps, and results, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.

translations.details.diagnostics.0: First confirm whether the controller needs full Jdot or just the product term of Jdot*qdot.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Zero out qddot and run forward kinematics to make the frame's classical acceleration correspond to the velocity drift term.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: When only the product term is needed, call forwardKinematics with zero qddot and use getFrameClassicalAcceleration() to read the frame's classical acceleration drift, avoiding explicit construction of Jdot.
translations.details.environments.0: 2021 Pinocchio API, two-degree-of-freedom arm example; original post lacks version, OS, or complete code.
translations.details.limits.0: No thread provides full function call order, reference frame parameter, or numerical output; the target version should be verified with the smallest test case.
translations.details.limits.1: This shortcut only answers Jdot*qdot, not the full Jdot matrix; if full Jdot is needed, use the corresponding API or derivation.
translations.details.limits.2: Users' own classical dJ formulas without maintainer confirmation are not included in the answer.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The original author confirmed understanding and adoption of this approach; maintainers confirm it is simple and efficient.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: When only the product term of classical Jdot*qdot is needed, is explicit calculation of the classical Jacobian time derivative necessary?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before applying drift compensation to real systems, validate the sign, frame, and units via numerical differentiation or known trajectory; incorrect bias will directly alter the expected joint acceleration.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The issue arises from mixing spatial Jacobian derivative with classical point acceleration control formulas.
translations.details.symptoms.0: getFrameJacobianTimeVariation returns spatial acceleration-related quantities, but the controller formula qddot_des = pinv(J)(ac_des - Jdot*qdot) requires the classical acceleration drift.
